name: Cron Abuse - Writable Script + pspy
description: Use pspy to watch for root cron jobs without root, then abuse a world-writable script they run by appending a reverse shell. Back up the original first.

steps.label: 2. Append reverse shell to the script

defense.why_it_works: Cron jobs run as root on a schedule and often reference scripts or files writable by low-privileged users. pspy monitors /proc without root privileges to reveal the exact commands being executed by cron, exposing writable script paths. Modifying those scripts inserts attacker code executed as root when the cron job fires.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access as a low-privileged user. A cron job running as root that references a file writable by the attacker's user. pspy binary transferred to the target.
defense.impact: Arbitrary command execution as root at the next cron cycle (often within 1–5 minutes). Attacker can add SUID shells, append to /etc/sudoers, install reverse shells, or exfiltrate /etc/shadow.
defense.detection: File integrity monitoring (Tripwire, AIDE, inotifywait) on cron-referenced scripts. Auditd: write to /dmz-backups/backup.sh by non-root user. SIEM: unexpected shell spawned from cron parent process (crond).
defense.artifacts: File integrity alert (cron script modified) | Auditd write event on cron-referenced script | Bash reverse shell connection in network logs
defense.prevention: Ensure all files referenced by root cron jobs are owned by root and not world/group writable. Use absolute paths in cron scripts. Run cron jobs as least-privilege service accounts rather than root where possible. Audit cron jobs with: for f in /etc/cron*; do ls -la $f; done.
defense.misconfiguration: Root cron job references /dmz-backups/backup.sh which is owned by a low-privileged user or is world-writable. The cron job runs as root (CRONTAB has no user field or specifies root).
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Vulnerable crontab
*/01 * * * * cd /home/htb-student && tar -zcf /home/htb-student/backup.tar.gz *
# Or: root cron runs /dmz-backups/backup.sh

# Insecure permissions
-rwxrwxrwx 1 root root /dmz-backups/backup.sh
defense.secure_config:
# Secure cron script ownership and permissions
chown root:root /dmz-backups/backup.sh
chmod 700 /dmz-backups/backup.sh

# Audit cron-referenced files
awk '{print $6}' /etc/crontab | xargs -I{} ls -la {} 2>/dev/null

# Run cron jobs as dedicated service account, not root
defense.evasion: pspy operates entirely through /proc -- no root required, no files written, no network traffic. Attacker appears to be running a benign background process.
